description: Exact-construction ReLU gadgets — fixed-weight sub-nets that compute a KNOWN continuous-piecewise-linear (CPWL) function. The cortex picks one of these when a target is a known formula instead of an unknown statistical function; render_to_weights materialises the weight matrices directly from the gadget's attrs. NO TRAINING. Source: §2.1 of docs/net_construction_techniques.md (Arora-style ReLU = CPWL representation; Garcia-Alvarez et al. 2025 construction methodology).
category_inheritance: genlMt → neural_networks (NN vocabulary) and → compiler_theory (continuity/soundness predicates — §2.6 of the doc).

concepts.name: cpwl_function
concepts.definition: Continuous piecewise-linear function. Exactly representable by a finite ReLU network — Arora et al. (ICLR 2018). The constructible territory.

concepts.name: gadget
concepts.definition: Fixed-weight ReLU sub-network computing a specific CPWL function. Constructed once from a formula, reused without retraining.

concepts.name: exact_construction
concepts.definition: Rendering a held formula directly into weights. The opposite of gradient descent: starts from understanding, not from a random init seeking the end.

concepts.name: polarization
concepts.definition: x·y = ½·((x+y)² − x² − y²). Reduces multiplication to squaring; the gateway from §2.1 primitives to §2.4 polynomials (lifted in a follow-up turn).

concepts.name: fold_construction
concepts.definition: Reuse one fold gadget at depth L to get 2^L linear pieces of x². The depth/precision trick from §2.3 (not implemented yet — referenced by net_construction_techniques.md).

gadgets.name: identity_gadget
gadgets.definition: f(x) = x via x = ReLU(x) − ReLU(−x). Emulates a skip connection in a strictly-feedforward ReLU net.
gadgets.mechanism: Layer 1 splits x into [ReLU(x), ReLU(−x)]; layer 2 takes the difference.
gadgets.tradeoff: Two hidden units for a pass-through — wasteful when residual connections are available. Useful as a building block when they aren't.

gadgets.name: abs_gadget
gadgets.definition: f(x) = |x| via |x| = ReLU(x) + ReLU(−x). The canonical one-layer ReLU construction.
gadgets.mechanism: Layer 1 splits x into [ReLU(x), ReLU(−x)]; layer 2 sums them.
gadgets.tradeoff: Discontinuous derivative at 0; for smooth abs use Huber or the soft-abs variant.

gadgets.name: max_gadget
gadgets.definition: f(x, y) = max(x, y) via max(x, y) = ReLU(x − y) + y. One hidden layer with 3 units (one for ReLU(x−y), two to reconstruct y as ReLU(y) − ReLU(−y) so layer 2 can be a pure linear without depending on input bias).
gadgets.mechanism: hidden = [ReLU(x − y), ReLU(y), ReLU(−y)]; output = hidden[0] + hidden[1] − hidden[2] = ReLU(x − y) + y.
gadgets.tradeoff: Three hidden units instead of two; the extra dim lets us avoid bias-depends-on-input.

gadgets.name: min_gadget
gadgets.definition: f(x, y) = min(x, y) via min(x, y) = −ReLU(y − x) + y. Mirror of max_gadget.
gadgets.mechanism: hidden = [ReLU(y − x), ReLU(y), ReLU(−y)]; output = −hidden[0] + hidden[1] − hidden[2] = −ReLU(y − x) + y.
gadgets.tradeoff: Same width/depth as max_gadget; produced as a parallel pair when both min and max are needed.

gadgets.name: abs_2d_gadget
gadgets.definition: Parallel application of |·| to each dim of a 2-vector: f([x, y]) = [|x|, |y|]. Two abs_gadgets composed laterally as width — §2.7 of the construction doc.
gadgets.mechanism: hidden = [ReLU(x), ReLU(−x), ReLU(y), ReLU(−y)]; output = [hidden[0]+hidden[1], hidden[2]+hidden[3]] = [|x|, |y|]. Block-diagonal W1 + block-diagonal W2.
gadgets.tradeoff: Block-diagonal structure wastes parameters relative to a fused implementation; clarity wins.

gadgets.name: abs_3d_gadget
gadgets.definition: Parallel application of |·| to each dim of a 3-vector: f([a, b, c]) = [|a|, |b|, |c|]. Block-diagonal expansion of abs_gadget × 3 (§2.7 width composition). Renders to (6×3, 6, 3×6, 3) weights at construct time — declared structurally; not hand-coded.
gadgets.mechanism: construct_weights reads parallel_of=abs_gadget, expands its W1/b1/W2/b2 block-diagonally to 3 copies, emits 4 WeightTensors.
gadgets.tradeoff: Block-diagonal structure makes the parallel application obvious in the weights; a fused implementation could save parameters at the cost of clarity.

gadgets.name: square_pwl_10_3d_gadget
gadgets.definition: Parallel application of square_pwl_10_gadget to each dim of a 3-vector on [0, 1]³: f([a, b, c]) ≈ [a², b², c²]. Block-diagonal expansion of square_pwl_10 × 3. The block-diagonal expansion of a width-10 primitive gives a 30-hidden-unit layer.
gadgets.mechanism: construct_weights reads parallel_of=square_pwl_10_gadget, expands its W1/b1/W2/b2 block-diagonally to 3 copies, emits 4 WeightTensors.
gadgets.tradeoff: Same accuracy bound as the 1D version (error ≤ 0.25%); three times the parameters.
gadgets.formula: f([a, b, c]) ≈ [a², b², c²] for a, b, c ∈ [0, 1]

gadgets.name: square_pwl_10_gadget
gadgets.definition: Piecewise-linear approximation of f(x) = x² on [0, 1] with 10 breakpoints. One ReLU layer, width 10, error ≤ 1/(4·N²) = 0.25% at midpoints of segments, exact at every breakpoint k/10. The CPWL way to approximate any smooth function — Arora et al. (2018) plus a standard secant-line construction.
gadgets.mechanism: y = Σ_k slope_change_k · ReLU(x − k/N). Slope_change is 1/N at the origin and 2/N at every subsequent break, since x² has constant second-derivative 2 and Δslope per Δx of 1/N gives 2/N.
gadgets.tradeoff: Width N for error O(1/N²) — linear cost in width, polynomial precision. The §2.3 fold construction trades width for depth (exponential pieces at linear depth).
gadgets.formula: f(x) ≈ x² for x ∈ [0, 1], width-10 PWL, error ≤ 0.25%

gadgets.name: square_pwl_signed_gadget
gadgets.definition: Approximation of f(x) = x² for x ∈ [−1, 1] via composition: |x| (abs_gadget) then PWL square (square_pwl_10_gadget). Since x² = |x|², the abs reduces signed input to [0, 1] where the PWL approximation applies. Two-step composed gadget, total ~12 hidden units.
gadgets.mechanism: Stage 1: abs_gadget reduces signed x to |x| ∈ [0, 1]. Stage 2: square_pwl_10_gadget approximates |x|² = x².
gadgets.tradeoff: Adds one layer of depth to handle sign; alternative is symmetric construction with breakpoints at ±k/N (also workable, more parameters).

gadgets.name: monomial_lift_step1_gadget
gadgets.definition: Fan-out step: [x] → [x, |x|]. Two LEAF gadgets (identity_gadget and abs_gadget) both see the full input x and write to consecutive output slots. The cpwl_broadcast kind: stack the W1s vertically (both rows of W1 read the same input column), block-diagonalize the W2s (each branch's output lands in its own slot).
gadgets.mechanism: construct_weights stacks [identity.W1; abs.W1] vertically to share input; b1 stacked; W2 block-diagonal so outputs land at separate slots; b2 stacked. Result: hidden_dim=4, dim_out=2.
gadgets.tradeoff: Limited to leaf branches (cpwl_primitive/cpwl_linear); composed branches need their own step structure.

gadgets.name: monomial_lift_step2_gadget
gadgets.definition: Per-slot step: [x, |x|] → [x, x²]. Two LEAF gadgets (identity_gadget on slot 0, square_pwl_10_gadget on slot 1) each read their own input slice. The cpwl_heteroparallel kind: block-diagonal W1 (each branch reads its slice), b1 stacked, block-diagonal W2, b2 stacked. Generalises cpwl_parallel to different sub-gadgets at each block.
gadgets.mechanism: construct_weights places identity.W1 (slot 0) and square_pwl_10.W1 (slot 1) on the diagonal blocks of W1; assembles W2 block-diagonally so each branch's output lands at its own slot.
gadgets.tradeoff: Same as cpwl_broadcast — leaf branches only.

gadgets.name: monomial_lift_x_x2_gadget
gadgets.definition: Lift x to the pair [x, x²]. Two-step composition: fan-out [x] → [x, |x|] then per-slot [x, |x|] → [x, x²]. Valid for x ∈ [−1, 1]; the abs reduces signed input to [0, 1] where square_pwl_10 is accurate. Used to feed downstream gadgets that need BOTH x and x² (e.g. polarization multiplication for cube).
gadgets.tradeoff: Two layers for the lift; depth scales with monomial degree if we want [x, x², x³, …].

gadgets.name: cube_gadget
gadgets.definition: f(x) ≈ x³ via the chain [monomial_lift_x_x2_gadget → polarization_multiply_gadget]. Lift x to [x, x²], then multiply via polarization to get x · x² = x³. Valid for x ∈ [−0.5, 0.5] so |x| + |x²| ≤ 0.75 ≤ 1 (polarization's domain).
gadgets.mechanism: Stage 1: monomial_lift_x_x2_gadget lifts [x] to [x, x²]. Stage 2: polarization_multiply_gadget computes the product. Net depth = lift_depth + polarization_depth = 2 + 4 = 6 ReLU layers.
gadgets.tradeoff: Six layers for one cube. The follow-up is monomial_lift_x_x2_x3 = lift then [identity_passthrough || cube_gadget], unlocking x⁴ via polarization, and so on by recursion.

gadgets.name: polarization_inputs_gadget
gadgets.definition: Affine map [x, y] → [x+y, x, y]. Three lanes of input to the polarization identity. Realised as cpwl_linear — the constructor expands W·x + b to a 2-layer ReLU using the identity-trick ReLU(W·x+b) − ReLU(−(W·x+b)).
gadgets.mechanism: W = [[1,1],[1,0],[0,1]] sends [x,y] to [x+y,x,y]; expanded by construct_weights to a 6-hidden-unit ReLU layer.
gadgets.tradeoff: Identity-trick doubles hidden width relative to a true linear layer; pays for staying in the ReLU-MLP shape end-to-end.

gadgets.name: polarization_combine_gadget
gadgets.definition: Affine map [a, b, c] → ½(a − b − c). With [a, b, c] = [(x+y)², x², y²], the output is ½((x+y)² − x² − y²) = x·y — the polarization identity that converts three squares into a multiplication.
gadgets.mechanism: W = [[0.5, −0.5, −0.5]]; expanded via the identity-trick to a 2-hidden-unit ReLU layer.
gadgets.tradeoff: None of substance — single linear projection.
gadgets.formula: f([a, b, c]) = ½·(a − b − c)

gadgets.name: polarization_multiply_gadget
gadgets.definition: Multiplication via the polarization identity (§2.4): x·y = ½·((x+y)² − x² − y²). Four-step chain: [polarization_inputs → abs_3d → square_pwl_10_3d → polarization_combine]. Valid for x, y ∈ [−0.5, 0.5] (so x+y ∈ [−1, 1]). Error inherited from square_pwl: ≤ 1/(4·N²) per square, halved by the polarization coefficient — empirically ≤ 0.004 on the test grid.
gadgets.mechanism: Stage 1: linear map [x,y] → [x+y, x, y]. Stage 2: parallel abs gives [|x+y|, |x|, |y|]. Stage 3: parallel square approximates [(x+y)², x², y²]. Stage 4: linear combines ½(s₁ − s₂ − s₃) = xy.
gadgets.tradeoff: Three squares for one multiplication — uneconomical at runtime but the recipe is queryable and the weights are exact. Tracr/RASP-style.

gadgets.name: max_abs_2d_gadget
gadgets.definition: f([x, y]) = max(|x|, |y|). Two-step composition: abs_2d_gadget then max_gadget. Demonstrates §2.7 layer-stacking — function composition equals depth.
gadgets.mechanism: Stage 1: abs_2d_gadget produces [|x|, |y|] (2 hidden layers internally). Stage 2: max_gadget on [|x|, |y|] produces max(|x|, |y|). Layer-stacked, no shared weights.
gadgets.tradeoff: Two full sub-networks chained; an optimized fused form would have fewer parameters but the same depth.
